Short answer: only if your gaming scenario would be CPU bottlenecked.

Long ver:

Taking data from GN's 2 recent reviews, the Intel 12th gen GPU revisit and the B570 review:
        Baldur's Gate 3 B580: w/9800x3d ~74 avg fps vs w/12400 ~63 avg fps vs w/5600x ~55 avg fps
but also consider that:
        Baldur's Gate 3: i5 12400 @1440p Ultra scored: ~79 avg fps /w RTX4060  while same CPU @1080p Medium : ~81 avg fps w/RTX 4090
        Baldur's Gate 3: r5 5600x @1440p Ultra scored: ~79 avg fps /w RTX4060  while same CPU @1080p Medium : ~81 avg fps w/RTX 4090
Yes, it's CPU limited enough that even an RTX4090 scored the same/similar avg fps for these two CPUs as the RTX4060 for this test; the 12400 having improved and better 1% and 0.1% low with the RTX4090 vs the R5 5600x at the lower setting/resolution. Baldur's gate 3 test were CPU limited enough that even if you lower setting & resolution AND upgraded to an RTX4090 it wouldn't improve the fps if you have these i5/r5.

Comparing to the FF 14 results as example of a GPU limited scenario: i5 12400 @1440p Max : ~96 avg fps /w RX7700xt, ~85 avg fps /w B580, ~72 avg fps /w RTX4060 and roughly the same avg fps with a 9800x3d for these GPUs while the same i5 @1080p Max: ~199fps /w RTX4090 (~151fps /w RX7700xt; ~120fps /w B580; ~112fps /w RTX4060).

Or the Cyberpunk @1080p Ultra results which the B580 scored the same avg/1%/0.1% on all 3 CPUs 9800x3d, 12400 and 5600x; similarly to the RTX4060, RX7600.

Yes, there is overhead issue on the Intel cards/drivers causing them to be more heavily penalized in CPU bottleneck scenario, a very valid point of concern for those with i3/r3 budget build; but I do not think it's the doomsday, end of the world scenario like some content creators would have you believe.
